answer: Each AI agent registers by locking a TPM-backed secure enclave identity whose private key is permanently fused inside the chip; the network sends hourly remote attestation challenges, and the registrar records every valid public key on a public ledge, so one physical chip cannot back two identities. An attacker who wants a million sybils must purchase and run a million separate enclave chips at about fifteen dollars each, because the crystal-clear attestation cannot be forged and there is no ivory-tower path that avoids the hardware cost.
